title: Погром в баре  (Chaos at the Bar)

segments.t: At the Claude Monet bar, Kostya is horrified to find shattered glass everywhere and six bottles of elite cognac missing or broken while Ainura mops the floor. Listen to the whole exchange first, and then we will break it down line by line.
У тебя неудачное шоу в баре?
Забыли закрыть, и ночью кто-то забрался.
Now let's go back through their conversation line by line and unpack the Russian phrasing.
'Kostya, what happened here?' Max presses straight out before Kostya can change the subject.
У тебя неудачное шоу в баре?
'Did you have a bad bartender show?' Focusing on the show on the spot, Max brings in "neudachnoye" ("unsuccessfully", from "neudachno") as the key Russian word here.
'I will find out who was juggling here at night.' Emphasizing the night at once, Kostya brings in "zhongliroval" ("juggled", from "zhonglirovat") as the key Russian word here.
'Ainura, could you clean up faster?' Kostya inquires firmly what Ainura is actually getting at here.
'Listen, Kostya, do not bother me.' Ainura steps in sharply right here and lands on "slushay" ("listen", built on "slushat") to keep the statement grounded.

'Let me breathe in the expensive cognac a bit.' Mentioning the expensive cognac beside Kostya, Ainura reaches for the Russian word "konyakom" ("cognac", built from "konyak") right at the center of the line.
'They smashed three bottles last night.' Kostya replies calmly without any doubt, steering the talk right where he wants it.
'Maybe only two bottles?' Turning to the bottle at once, Max centers the thought on "butylki" ("bottle", from "butylka") without wasting a word.
'No, not two, three.' Kostya counters wryly in this moment, steering the talk right where he wants it.
Забыли закрыть, и ночью кто-то забрался.
'They forgot to lock up, and someone broke in at night.' Kostya pushes back dryly in their talk, leaving no doubt about where he stands.
'Who could have done that?' Max answers naturally in this beat and chooses "sdelat" ("to do") so Kostya gets the point right away.
'Well of course, not me.' Kostya reacts promptly at once and leans on "konechno" ("of course") to give the whole sentence its punch.
'And what are you doing here?' Ainura wonders frankly if there is more going on behind the scenes.
У тебя неудачное шоу в баре?
Забыли закрыть, и ночью кто-то забрался.
Max suddenly realizes why there were two extra bottles in Katya's apartment. Next, Chef Barinov walks in with a massive hangover of his own. Until next time!
